summary.text: Mosses are small, flowerless plants in the division Bryophyta that are non-vascular and typically form dense green clumps or mats.
They reproduce with spores rather than seeds, and the haploid gametophyte is the dominant phase of their life cycle.
Threadlike rhizoids anchor them, and their simple leaves are usually just one cell thick.

facts.label: Main commercial use
facts.value: The main constituent of peat, mostly Sphagnum

items.prompt: A shop sells 'Iceland moss' gathered from a mountain, and a botanist says the name misleads. What does she say it really is?

options.label: A giant moss that grows to 60 centimetres
A liverwort, the closest relative of true mosses
A lichen, which is a symbiotic colony and not related to mosses
A fern whose leaves stay tightly curled

items.explain: Lichens may resemble mosses and share common names, but they are symbiotic colonies and not related to mosses.

items.prompt: A gardener peels a green mat off a stone and finds fine threads holding it on. What are the threads most like?

options.label: Root hairs rather than the thick roots of seed plants
Taproots that reach deep into the stone
Seeds waiting for rain to sprout
Spore stalks, each topped with a capsule

items.explain: Mosses anchor with threadlike rhizoids, comparable to root hairs rather than the more substantial roots of seed plants.

items.prompt: The soft green carpet on a shaded log is mostly which phase of the moss life cycle?

options.label: The diploid sporophyte, as in seed plants
Equal parts gametophyte and sporophyte
The sporophyte capsules on their stalks
The haploid gametophyte, which has a single set of chromosomes

items.explain: In mosses the haploid gametophyte is the dominant phase. Only the sporophyte stage has paired chromosomes, and it is short-lived.

items.prompt: A gardener wants more moss and collects what drops from the plants at the end of the season. What will she actually gather?

options.label: Seeds from tiny flowers
Spores from capsules on unbranched stalks
Pollen-covered fruits
Bulbs from the base of the stem

items.explain: Mosses reproduce with spores, not seeds, and have no flowers. The spores sit in single capsules on unbranched stalks.

items.prompt: A garden-supply firm wants to sell the moss product with the biggest commercial role. What should it stock?

options.label: Edible flour ground from the dried plants
Thread spun into cotton-like fabric
Peat, made mostly from the genus Sphagnum
Cooking oil pressed from the capsules

items.explain: The main commercial significance of mosses is as the main constituent of peat, mostly Sphagnum.

items.prompt: Under a lens a botanist sees a small plant with a clear stem, simple leaves and rhizoids made of many cells. Which group, rather than its look-alike the liverwort, does this point to?

options.label: A moss
A hornwort
A lichen
A liverwort

items.explain: Mosses have multi-cellular rhizoids, unlike liverworts, and a clearly differentiated stem with simple non-vascular leaves points to a moss.
